feed.title: stackwith.me Field Notes
feed.subtitle: Practical notes on browser rendering, reliability, and interface design from Joel Ryan's workshop.

entry.title: Label a prototype so readers can evaluate the real work
entry.summary: Use AXON to separate live interface behavior, simulated data, design targets, and unavailable actions, with a practical copy and review method.

entry.title: Camera smoothing: exponential damping or a spring?
entry.summary: Compare two camera-follow models with a working response plot, a frame-rate-independent damping formula, and an exact critically damped spring step.

entry.title: Browser multiplayer with Supabase: transport, state, and trust
entry.summary: Follow Signal Strike’s relay and browser-host design, work through snapshot interpolation and message counts, and identify which guarantees the architecture cannot provide.

entry.title: Three.js instancing: what one draw call actually means
entry.summary: Build a valid instance batch, use per-instance attributes, and account for geometry families, shadows, and animated bounds when counting rendering work.

entry.title: A WebGL quality governor that measures its own limits
entry.summary: Inspect the Lab’s real quality thresholds, calculate the pixel cost of DPR, and distinguish frame pacing from GPU time before changing rendering quality.

entry.title: Ship compressed 3D assets without breaking colour or coordinates
entry.summary: Follow the repository’s Blender, Draco, and KTX2 pipeline, inspect actual file sizes, and avoid double colour conversion, axis errors, and misleading compression claims.

entry.title: A browser chime with a real start, stop, and voice limit
entry.summary: Build an opt-in Web Audio chime with an envelope, explicit cleanup, and bounded overlap, using the Lab’s actual sound graph as a reference.

entry.title: Test a WebGL page without mistaking a hook for proof
entry.summary: Use browser diagnostics, bounded polling, rendered inspection, and recorded source versions to distinguish a successful build from a working WebGL experience.

entry.title: Make a WebGL page useful when the scene cannot run
entry.summary: Build the reading page first, enhance it after a real frame, and handle disabled scripts, reduced motion, failed assets, and lost graphics contexts.

entry.title: Design an action record that can explain an uncertain outcome
entry.summary: Work through a proposed publishing action, distinguish intent from execution, and design an audit record that handles timeouts, retries, redaction, and verification.

entry.title: Turn a latency headline into a testable budget
entry.summary: Define a hand-off boundary, allocate a hypothetical 40 ms budget, and plan percentile measurements without presenting a design target as a production result.

entry.title: Make an approval mean one specific action
entry.summary: Design an approval contract around a resource, revision, scope, and expiry; then handle changed inputs, revocation, duplicate requests, and uncertain execution.
